title: Skeleton SOTA AI Application Construction Contract
purpose: Canonical machine-readable build manual for constructing, assembling, validating, operating, and evolving the complete AI application without architecture gaps.

provider_bootstrap.rule: Every AI development agent and every credential-bearing AI provider activation must load the active architecture, construction, capability-interface, and manual contracts before changing or serving the system.

quality_attributes.correctness: Contract-first boundaries, deterministic validators, typed provider-neutral interfaces, evidence-backed release gates.
quality_attributes.availability: Bounded retries, circuit breaking, graceful degradation, durable checkpoints, provider failover, recovery drills.
quality_attributes.latency: Fast-path routing, streaming, caches, async I/O, parallel validation, isolated accelerators, budget-aware model selection.
quality_attributes.security: Least privilege, sealed secrets, SSRF-safe provider endpoints, input/output bounds, sandboxed tools, auditable authority.
quality_attributes.privacy: Explicit data classes, minimization, retention/deletion policy, tenant isolation, provider privacy ceilings.
quality_attributes.observability: Request/trace correlation, structured logs, metrics, cost/latency/quality telemetry, SLOs and evidence receipts.
quality_attributes.evolvability: Canonical owners, adapters before migrations, capability contracts, compatibility windows, architecture drift gates.

construction_phases.goal: Freeze canonical contracts and bootstrap rules before implementation.
Establish identity, persistence, security and observability required by every higher plane.
Make provider execution neutral, declared, measurable, bounded and routable.

Produce reproducible, observable, reversible production releases.
Evolve by measured domain changes while preserving all contracts.

cognitive_runtime_blueprint.objective: Specify the exact runtime, state, contracts, recovery, safety and evidence semantics required for one fully functional AI execution path without introducing a second orchestration framework.

contracts.rule: immutable/provider-neutral value contracts only; no provider SDK, database client, HTTP transport or tool implementation imports

runtime.rule: the only engine module allowed to coordinate repeated model->tool->model turns for product operations

repository.rule: storage-neutral interface plus production Mongo adapter; no orchestration policy

adds: canonical ToolManifest projection for model exposure
tool_boundary.rule: a model can propose a tool call but cannot grant itself authority or bypass execution policy

stream_adapter.rule: transport projects committed operation events and never becomes state authority

frontend_reducer.rule: client state is reconstructable from authoritative operation/result APIs plus replayable events

state_rules: execution state refines but never replaces OperationState
OperationState is the user-visible lifecycle authority
execution states are durable substate required for exact recovery
terminal execution state and terminal OperationState must agree
tool_pending/tool_completed map through OperationState.WAITING_FOR_TOOL or RUNNING as appropriate
repairing and provider retries remain bounded by the original StopPolicy

identity: execution_id is stable for the full operation execution attempt
turn_id is globally unique and immutable
turn_index starts at zero and is strictly monotonic inside one execution
parent_turn_id forms a single canonical lineage for serial turns
parallel tool children use call_id lineage but do not create competing model-turn parents
turn_contract.invariant: the exact inputs necessary to explain a model turn are addressable by immutable ids/digests even when raw sensitive content is retained elsewhere

normalization: reject unknown or duplicate call ids
validate structured output against declared JSON-schema-equivalent contract
bound raw response size before parsing
preserve provider request id and usage without preserving credentials

may_repair: syntactically invalid tool arguments when schema-safe repair is possible
repair_policy.rule: repair consumes the same original execution budget and creates a new AgentTurn

ordering: tool results from the current execution
trust_marking: system instructions are trusted control data
user content is untrusted task data
memory preserves provenance and never upgrades trust
budgeting: reserve output budget before context packing
reserve tool-result headroom when tools are enabled
trim by deterministic priority then recency then relevance
summaries are derived state and keep source ids
never trim mandatory policy, authority, stop-policy or operation identity
compaction: compaction may replace old conversational text with a provenance-bearing summary
compaction cannot delete authoritative user/tool action receipts
summary generation is itself a metered model operation when a model is used
compaction output is untrusted until schema/invariant validation

authority_classes.write: requires explicit write authority and idempotency
authority_classes.destructive: requires explicit destructive authority plus approval policy

idempotency: completed call_id returns the durable prior receipt rather than executing again
in-progress reservation uses fencing/lease semantics to prevent concurrent duplicate execution
parallelism: parallel calls require no declared ordering dependency
parallel calls share the execution budget
results are joined deterministically by proposal order/call id
one failure cannot silently cancel already-committed sibling side effects

invariants: approval is bound to the exact tool arguments digest
edited arguments require a new approval
resume revalidates identity, policy, budget and deadline
approval never overrides restricted data-transfer or missing tool authority

prohibited: unverified model speculation presented as fact
tool output outside the principal's authority

qualified results surface uncertainty/provenance to the application
